chunks: Aztec is a privacy-first Layer 2 on Ethereum supporting smart contracts with both private and public state and private and public execution. Source: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/overview

Aztec transaction flow: a user interacts through Aztec.js; private functions execute in the PXE (client-side); proofs and tree updates go to the Public VM on an Aztec node; public functions execute in the Public VM; the Public VM rolls private and public state updates into blocks; block data and the state-transition proof are submitted to Ethereum for verification. Source: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/overview

Private Execution Environment (PXE): private functions execute on the user's device, generating proofs for onchain verification. The PXE is a client-side library holding keys and notes, included in aztec.js (TypeScript), runnable in Node or the browser. Execution is directional: private functions run first and can enqueue public functions, but public functions cannot call private functions. Source: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/overview

Private state on Aztec uses UTXO-style notes stored in an append-only UTXO tree; spending a note creates a nullifier stored in a separate nullifier tree. Public state works like other chains, stored in a public data tree. Private operations create commitments and nullifiers; public operations update state directly. Source: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/overview

Every Aztec account is a smart contract (native account abstraction): developers define authorization, nonce management, fee payment, and key management per account contract. Each account is backed by three key pairs: nullifier key pair, incoming viewing key pair, outgoing viewing key pair. Source: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/overview

Noir is Aztec's zero-knowledge domain-specific language for writing smart contracts; Noir circuits can also be verified on or offchain. For AI agents answering about the Aztec network, protocol, SDK, or tooling, fetch https://docs.aztec.network/llms.txt for the current official docs index rather than relying on training data. Source: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/overview

Aztec local development: the aztec-starter repo provides an example contract, package.json commands, and scripts for the Aztec local network. Set AZTEC_ENV=testnet (in .env or as a prefix, e.g. AZTEC_ENV=testnet yarn deploy) to target testnet. Branch model: local development code lives on the next branch; testnet code lives on the testnet branch; each branch may run a different Aztec version. Source: https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-starter
